prompt: What are the default CDP advertisement interval and holdtime?
options: 60 seconds and 180 seconds
30 seconds and 120 seconds
60 seconds and 120 seconds
180 seconds and 60 seconds
explanation: CDP advertises every 60 seconds with a 180-second holdtime. A receiver ages out an entry when advertisements stop for that long.

whyWrong.2: The interval is 60 seconds, but the CDP holdtime is 180 seconds.
whyWrong.3: That reverses the interval and the holdtime.

exhibit.title: Representative SW1# show lldp neighbors
exhibit.text:
Capability codes: (R) Router, (B) Bridge, (T) Telephone, (S) Station
Device ID   Local Intf  Hold-time  Capability  Port ID
DIST1       Gi0/24     120        B           Te1/0/1

prompt: What does this LLDP output show?
options: DIST1 is advertising the LLDP station capability.
DIST1 advertises bridge capability and remote port Te1/0/1.
B means the receiving local port is blocked by STP.
The B code proves that DIST1 cannot also support routing.
explanation: In the LLDP capability legend, B means bridge, which covers Ethernet switching. The row maps local Gi0/24 to DIST1's remote port Te1/0/1.

whyWrong.2: The capability field shows the neighbor's capability, not the local STP state.
whyWrong.3: A bridge capability does not rule out routing.

prompt: Which command disables CDP on Gi0/2 only, entered under the interface?
options: no cdp run
no lldp transmit
no cdp enable
cdp timer 0
explanation: no cdp enable turns CDP off on one interface. Leave cdp run on globally so other ports keep working.

whyWrong.0: no cdp run is global and disables CDP on the whole device.
whyWrong.1: That changes LLDP, a different protocol.
whyWrong.3: A timer value does not enable or disable CDP on an interface.

prompt: Which two commands show the local CDP timer settings? (Choose two.)
options: show cdp neighbors detail
show cdp
show cdp interface
show ip route
explanation: show cdp lists the global CDP timers, and show cdp interface lists CDP status and timers per interface. Neighbor detail describes received entries, not local settings.

whyWrong.0: Neighbor detail shows a received entry, not the local timers.
whyWrong.3: The routing table has no CDP timer information.

prompt: What can LLDP-MED network-policy information tell a supported IP phone?
options: The phone's complete IPv4 address, subnet mask and default gateway.
The voice call server's successful registration response.
The switch's complete table of reachable IP subnets.
The intended voice VLAN and associated traffic-priority policy.
explanation: LLDP-MED network policy advertises the voice VLAN and its priority values to the phone. It does not replace IP configuration or the data path.

whyWrong.0: IP address, mask and gateway come from DHCP or static configuration.
whyWrong.1: LLDP-MED does not report call-server registration.
whyWrong.2: LLDP-MED does not exchange routing tables.

exhibit.title: Supplied endpoint evidence
exhibit.text:
PC-A has no CDP or LLDP agent
Its access link is up in the intended VLAN
PC-A and a same-subnet peer exchange repeated successful pings
Switch CDP/LLDP uplink neighbors refresh normally

prompt: PC-A passes traffic but never appears in the CDP or LLDP tables. What follows?
options: The user-traffic test is invalid because every host must advertise LLDP.
The access VLAN is inactive despite the successful local exchange.
The switch has proved PC-A's software is trustworthy.
Absence is expected for the stated host and does not contradict its traffic test.
explanation: A PC appears in these tables only if it runs CDP or LLDP. IP traffic works without either protocol.

whyWrong.0: Hosts need no discovery protocol to pass traffic.
whyWrong.1: The successful traffic test shows the VLAN is working.

exhibit.title: Representative SW1# show cdp neighbors
exhibit.text:
Device ID  Local Intrfce  Holdtme  Capability  Platform    Port ID
SW2        Gig 0/1       172      S I         WS-C2960-   Gig 0/2
R1         Gig 0/2       156      R S I       CISCO2911   Gig 0/0

prompt: These rows come from show cdp neighbors on SW1. Which link record is correct?
options: SW1 Gi0/2 → SW2 Gi0/1; SW1 Gi0/0 → R1 Gi0/2
SW1 Gi0/1 → SW2 Gi0/1; SW1 Gi0/2 → R1 Gi0/2
SW1 Gi0/1 → SW2 Gi0/2; SW1 Gi0/2 → R1 Gi0/0
SW2 Gi0/1 → R1 Gi0/0; SW1 Gi0/2 has no neighbor
explanation: Local Intrfce is SW1's own port, and Port ID is the neighbor's port. Read each row as local port to neighbor and its port.

whyWrong.0: This reverses the local and remote ports and invents SW1 Gi0/0.
whyWrong.1: The remote ports are not the same as the local port numbers.
whyWrong.3: The table shows two SW1 adjacencies and nothing about SW2 to R1.

exhibit.title: Recorded interface state on the connected ports
exhibit.text:
SW1 Gi0/1: LLDP Tx enabled; Rx enabled
SW2 Gi0/2: LLDP Tx disabled; Rx enabled

prompt: LLDP runs globally on both switches and the cable is good. What do the neighbor tables show?
options: Neither switch learns the other because LLDP requires bidirectional transmission.
Both switches learn each other because global enablement overrides interface settings.
SW1 learns SW2, but SW2 cannot learn SW1.
SW2 learns SW1, but SW1 cannot learn SW2.
explanation: A switch learns a neighbor only if that neighbor transmits and it receives. SW1 transmits, so SW2 learns SW1, while SW2 does not transmit, so SW1 learns nothing.

whyWrong.0: LLDP works one way, since transmit and receive are separate.
whyWrong.1: Global enablement does not override a disabled interface direction.

prompt: A fresh CDP entry lists SW2's management address 192.168.12.12, but SW1 cannot ping it. What is justified?
options: Discovery works; IP reachability requires separate checks.
The management path is working because discovery crossed the link.
The management address must be on the port facing SW1.
CDP authenticated SW2 and verified its SSH service.
explanation: CDP is a Layer 2 protocol. A CDP entry proves discovery, not IP reachability, so test the IP path separately.

whyWrong.1: A Layer 2 advertisement does not test the IP path.
whyWrong.2: A device can advertise an address from any of its interfaces.
whyWrong.3: CDP does not authenticate a device or test SSH.

prompt: Policy bans discovery on an untrusted provider-facing port. Internal links still need it. Which change fits?
options: Disable both discovery protocols globally on the switch.
Disable CDP on the port while leaving LLDP participation enabled.
Disable both discovery protocols on the port and preserve approved internal use.
Disable only LLDP transmission on the port and leave other discovery enabled.
explanation: Disable both CDP and LLDP on that interface only. Disabling just one still leaves discovery running, and a global change breaks internal links.

whyWrong.0: A global change removes discovery from approved internal links.
whyWrong.1: LLDP would still run on the provider port.
whyWrong.3: CDP and LLDP receive would still run there.

prompt: show lldp says LLDP is not enabled. You want it only on uplink Gi0/1. What do you configure?
options: Enter cdp run; LLDP automatically shares CDP’s state.
Enable lldp run, Gi0/1 transmit/receive, and verify port policy.
Add a default route; the LLDP process starts when a gateway is reachable.
Only enter lldp receive on Gi0/1; the global process can remain disabled.
explanation: LLDP needs the global lldp run and the interface lldp transmit and lldp receive. CDP and LLDP are configured separately.

whyWrong.0: CDP and LLDP are configured independently.
whyWrong.2: LLDP is Layer 2 and does not need a route.
whyWrong.3: An interface setting does not run LLDP while the global process is off.

prompt: The sender advertises a 180-second CDP holdtime. The receiver's countdown reads about 174 seconds. What does that mean?
options: The link has been down for exactly 174 seconds.
The sender will transmit its next advertisement in 174 seconds.
The neighbor was discovered for the first time 174 seconds ago.
About 6 seconds have elapsed since the advertisement that last refreshed this entry.
explanation: The countdown is the time left before the entry ages out, so 180 minus 174 is about 6 seconds since the last advertisement.

whyWrong.0: The countdown is time remaining, not link downtime.
whyWrong.1: It is the entry's lifetime, not the sender's schedule.
whyWrong.2: A refresh restarts the countdown, so it is not the time since first discovery.

prompt: The device has no cdp run, but Gi0/1 has cdp enable. What is the CDP state?
options: CDP remains disabled globally; the interface command does not override that.
Gi0/1 operates CDP while every other interface stays disabled.
Only CDP reception works on Gi0/1.
The device automatically changes to LLDP on Gi0/1.
explanation: CDP runs only when both the global setting and the interface setting allow it. no cdp run disables CDP everywhere.

whyWrong.1: An interface setting does not override the global state.
whyWrong.2: CDP has no separate receive-only mode here.
whyWrong.3: The device does not switch to LLDP on its own.

prompt: Two CDP neighbors are actually separated by an Ethernet hub. What do you document?
options: The hub must have an IP address in the CDP table before the observation can be valid.
Document the speakers and hub; discovery does not prove a single cable.
The hub is necessarily the Device ID shown in each CDP row.
Every unmanaged switch must forward LLDP in exactly the same way.
explanation: A hub repeats signals and does not run CDP, so it never appears in CDP output. Record the CDP speakers and the hub separately.

whyWrong.0: A hub needs no IP address to repeat signals.
whyWrong.2: Device ID is always the advertising device, not a hub in between.
whyWrong.3: Do not assume every unmanaged device behaves the same way.

exhibit.title: Supplied protocol checks
exhibit.text:
Physical connection up; intended interfaces verified
SW1: CDP enabled; LLDP globally disabled
SW2: LLDP globally enabled, Tx/Rx enabled; CDP disabled
Policy: use LLDP on this link

prompt: Both devices support CDP and LLDP, but the tables stay empty. SW1 uses CDP and SW2 uses LLDP. Which change gives LLDP discovery?
options: Change both management gateways to the same router address.
Enable CDP on SW2 while leaving SW1's LLDP disabled.
Enable LLDP globally and in both directions on SW1's connected port.
Clear both tables repeatedly while keeping their protocol settings.
explanation: The two devices run different discovery protocols and neither hears the other. Enable LLDP globally and on the port on SW1, in both directions.

whyWrong.0: A shared management gateway does not fix a protocol mismatch.
whyWrong.1: That gives CDP discovery, not the required LLDP.
whyWrong.3: Clearing tables does not change which protocol runs.

exhibit.title: Supplied complete relevant direction state
exhibit.text:
LLDP globally enabled on both devices; link up
SW1: transmit enabled, receive disabled
SW2: transmit disabled, receive enabled
Old entries have expired

prompt: SW1 must receive fresh SW2 information through LLDP. Which two interface changes are needed? (Choose two.)
options: Enable LLDP transmit on SW1.
Enable LLDP receive on SW1.
Enable LLDP receive on SW2.
Enable LLDP transmit on SW2.
Disable CDP on both switches.
explanation: SW2 must transmit and SW1 must receive. Those are the two directions currently disabled.

whyWrong.0: SW1 transmit is already on and sends in the other direction.
whyWrong.2: SW2 receive is already on and concerns learning SW1.

exhibit.title: Supplied maintenance records
exhibit.text:
09:00 drawing: SW1 Gi0/1 to SW2 Gi0/2
09:02 saved CDP record: same endpoints
09:10 cable move recorded, destination port not recorded
09:11 new SW1 LLDP record: neighbor name SW2, remote Gi0/1
No post-move SW2 observation or physical-port inspection has yet been recorded

prompt: An older record and a newer one-sided record disagree about the Gi0/1 neighbor. What do you do?
options: Replace the approved drawing with the oldest cached observation.
Record the disagreement and confirm current identities and both port ends before updating the drawing.
Declare Gi0/1 physically faulty because two records disagree.
Publish the new one-sided record immediately because it has the latest timestamp.
explanation: The two records were taken at different times and the new one has no second end. Confirm both ends and the neighbor's identity before you change the drawing.

whyWrong.0: The old record predates the move and may be wrong now.
whyWrong.2: Conflicting records do not show a physical fault.
whyWrong.3: The newest record still needs its other end confirmed.

prompt: What is the default LLDP state on a Catalyst switch?
options: Enabled globally and on every interface
Disabled
Enabled on trunk ports only
Enabled for receive only
explanation: LLDP is disabled by default on Catalyst switches. Enable it with lldp run.

whyWrong.0: That describes CDP, which is on by default.
whyWrong.2: The default does not depend on port type.
whyWrong.3: With LLDP disabled, neither direction runs.

prompt: Once LLDP is enabled, what are its default advertisement interval and holdtime?
options: 60 seconds and 180 seconds
30 seconds and 120 seconds
30 seconds and 180 seconds
60 seconds and 120 seconds
explanation: LLDP advertises every 30 seconds with a 120-second holdtime.

whyWrong.2: The LLDP holdtime is 120 seconds, not 180.
whyWrong.3: The LLDP interval is 30 seconds, not 60.

prompt: Which global command turns on LLDP?
options: cdp run
lldp enable
lldp run
lldp transmit
explanation: lldp run starts the LLDP process globally. lldp transmit and lldp receive are interface commands.

whyWrong.0: cdp run controls CDP, not LLDP.
whyWrong.1: lldp enable is not an IOS command.
whyWrong.3: lldp transmit is an interface command.

prompt: What is the default LLDP reinitialization delay?
options: 2 seconds
30 seconds
60 seconds
120 seconds
explanation: The LLDP reinitialization delay is 2 seconds by default.

whyWrong.2: 60 seconds is the CDP advertisement interval.
